reason: Rounded on the back (abaxial side) of a lemma, glume, seed or mericarp, as opposed to keeled, means convex there; 'dorsally' names the region of the bearer (surface or region pattern).

Ambiguous: 'sori embossed' means sunken sori showing as bumps on the other surface, while for epidermal cells and fruit it means a raised relief; no single quality fits, and 'raised' would be wrong for the sorus.
'Venation pinnate' of a leaf blade is the existing FLOPO value pinnately veined; 'obscurely' is a qualifier.

target: new: quality of the parts of a covering (floccose PATO_0104366 of the part + white PATO_0000323 of its trichomes PO_0000282)
reason: Two values with different bearers: the part is floccose, the hairs are white. Not a term.

target: new: quality of the parts of a covering (spiny PATO_0001365 of the part + antrorse PATO_0002238 of its prickles PO_0025169)
reason: Aculeolate = with small prickles (aculeate was mapped to spiny in the previous review); 'antrorsely' is the direction of the prickles, not of the leaf.
Amaranth as a flower colour is a purplish red; reddish purple is the nearest PATO colour (magenta PATO_0000321 is the alternative).
A testa marked by a network whose meshes are hexagonal; the quality is reticulate, and the hexagonal (PATO_0002509) meshes are a detail of the areoles, not a new term.
'With gland(s)' / 'com glândula(s)' states that glands are present; gland is a RELATED synonym of PO_0005656 (previous rule C265).
An absolute statement of a pale/light colour of bark or margins; PATO_0000665 has the synonym 'light'. Unlike 'lighter' it needs no second term.
Rhizomatous = bearing rhizomes, like 'stoloniferous' (C208); 'long' is a quality of the rhizome (increased length PATO_0000573) and can be added to it.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: ovate FLOPO:0991024 and cuneate PATO_0001955)
reason: A compound of two shape values, handled like 'linear-lanceolate' by the continuum relation, not by a term.
A part, not a quality; for flowers and inflorescences it is the PO receptacle. Fern sporangial receptacles should not be grounded to this flower part.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: 'upper' in config/flora_context_words.tsv) + docs/odp/02-bounded-measurement.md
reason: The length of the distal region of the pedicel, with a bound ('≤ 1 mm'); a region and a measurement, not a quality word.
Nonpeltate = not peltate, the negation of the existing FLOPO value, like 'unlobed' (C239).

label: laciniate-lepidote
definition: A scaly quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with small peltate scales whose margins are irregularly cut into narrow, fringe-like segments.
reason: A recurring indumentum type (Bromeliaceae), sibling of stellate-lepidote FLOPO:0991304, which the previous reviews made a class.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (attached to PATO_0001667 towards the named part)
reason: 'Fixed at the top of the column', 'fixed 4-7 mm above the base of the petiole' state attachment to another part; without that part the word is meaningless.
'Subtending bract' names a bract by its relation to the part it subtends, which is not given; a relation stated without its second term, as in the previous review.

target: new: quality of the parts of a covering (scaly PATO_0001804 of the part + brown PATO_0000952 of its scales)
reason: Lepidote = scaly (C235); brown is the colour of the scales, not of the part, and 'densely' is a degree qualifier.
A faint or partial brown colour; the colour is brown and 'tinged' is a degree qualifier kept in the record.

target: not ciliate (no term yet: needs a FLOPO value 'ciliate' under hairy PATO_0000454)
reason: Aciliate = margin not fringed with hairs, the negation of ciliate; neither PATO (ciliated PATO_0001408 is about cell cilia) nor the FLOPO values have 'ciliate' yet.
Negation of the existing value caespitose, which has the synonym cespitose.
A cross-sectional folding of the blade of a few taxa; doubtful as a general quality and unclear without the plane of section, so no term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between rounded/obtuse PATO_0001935 and cuneate PATO_0001955) on the leaf base
reason: A compound of two base shapes on the region 'base'; handled by the continuum relation, not a term.
A part: the stalk-like base of the flower whose length is given; stipe maps to stalk (C264).
A faint green colour; the colour is green and 'tinged' is a degree qualifier, as for 'tinged with brown'.

label: stem-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a stem: elongate, slender and cylindrical, not swollen.
reason: Used for orchid pseudobulbs and rhizomes that are not thickened; sibling of rhizome-like FLOPO:0991325 and stolon-like FLOPO:0991359.
'Veins not fusing' = veins not joining into loops; all examples are negated, and the positive sense is anastomosing.
Square with 'nearly' as the approximate qualifier (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md).

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (sorus located next to the costule)
reason: A position of the sorus relative to the costule (pinna-segment midrib), a relation to another part rather than a term.
A spelling variant of the existing value gland-dotted.
